facts.claim: Micro-influencer campaigns work most effectively when they encourage active brand engagement rather than depending only on perceived attractiveness, trustworthiness, or parasocial familiarity.
facts.quote: the condensed paper therefore argues that micro-influencer campaigns work most effectively when they encourage active brand engagement rather than depending only on perceived attractiveness, trustworthiness, or parasocial familiarity.

facts.claim: Micro-influencers who are believed to be genuine and more trustworthy affect consumer buying decisions more than macro-influencers.
facts.quote: It is found that micro-influencers who are believed to be genuine and more trustworthy, affect consumer buying decisions more than macro-influencers who have a wide reach but may not be seen as genuine enough.

facts.claim: Micro-influencers significantly impact consumer decision-making by leveraging their relatability and perceived authenticity to foster deeper emotional connections.
facts.quote: Findings reveal that micro-influencers significantly impact consumer decision-making, leveraging their relatability and perceived authenticity to foster deeper emotional connections.

facts.claim: Online interaction with a brand because of micro-influencer endorsements is linked to purchase intention.
facts.quote: one variable emerges as significant: online interaction with a brand because of micro-influencer endorsements positively predicts purchase intention.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: Micro-influencers differ significantly from others in terms of their interaction power and perceived high credibility in social media marketing.
facts.quote: It has been concluded that micro-influencers differ significantly from others in terms of their interaction power and perceived high credibility in social media marketing.

research.angle: While micro-influencers drive deeper emotional connections and purchase intentions through relatability and interaction, their effectiveness depends specifically on active brand engagement rather than just perceived trustworthiness.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that micro-influencers are more effective than macro-influencers at driving consumer behavior due to perceived authenticity and interaction power.
research.caveat: The research is limited by small sample sizes, a focus on specific social media platforms, and a lack of theoretical integration across different platforms.
